correctness.rationale: For each block of P, every nonempty Q rectangle lies in a single P rectangle by the disjoint-row/disjoint-column definition; the Q deletions within it create m paired row/column types plus optional unmatched row/column types. Row and column duplication leaves complex Schur norm unchanged via weighted trace-norm formula; disjoint output blocks give sup norms, including countable finite-compression exhaustion. The canonical masks D_m^{u,v} exhaust the possibilities. Using Levene weighted trace-class duality and automorphism-averaging lemmas, the three scalar optimizations are D_m^{00}=2-2/m, D_m^{10}=m/sqrt(2m-1) for m=2,3 and baseline otherwise, D_m^{11}=(m-1+2m sqrt(m+2))/(4m-1) for m<=4 and baseline thereafter (with m=1 and zero cases treated). Fresh numerical scalar maximizations independently corroborate these threshold branches for m<=8; closed differentiation and concavity, not grid sampling, prove all m. Infinite J-I attains norm 2 by finite compression; no other limit point is possible. The conclusion is for complex operator Schur norm, not Schatten p-norm or positive sums.
